text:
After 20 years of unbroken loyalty as a Bonitas member, I will be leaving the scheme—and moving my parents off their Bonitas option, which I pay for, as well—due to ongoing, dangerous delays with your designated chronic medication courier, Marara Pharmacy, and a general collapse in service quality from Service Providers.

Since Bonitas's administrator move, the service across the board has deteriorated. I have dealt with numerous issues with other service providers (which I won't even go into detail about here), painfully long response times—or a complete lack of response—from both Bonitas and its service providers, and constant problems with the Bonitas website, member portal, and app that still haven't been sorted out.

However, the chronic medication delays are what pushed me over the edge. Managing chronic conditions is stressful enough without your medical aid's appointed service provider repeatedly leaving you without essential medication:
• July 2026: I had to send urgent emails warning that I was down to my last 1–2 chronic tablets.

• September 2026: I was forced to follow up on a Sunday night because I only had a single blood pressure tablet left for the next day.

• November 2026: This was the final straw. According to the medication label, my parcel was processed on 3 November (and possibly prepared even earlier), yet it was never dispatched. When I flagged on Thursday, 5 November that I only had enough blood pressure medication left for Friday, I was told delivery arrangements would only be finalised on Monday due to "requirements" on other items on my script. Instead of dispatching the ready, urgently needed blood pressure medication, the entire order was held back. Because this was the final repeat on my prescription, I didn't even have a script to take to a local retail pharmacy to buy an emergency supply over the weekend. My parcel only arrived the following Tuesday/Wednesday, leaving me completely without blood pressure medication for 4 to 5 days.

While I was fortunate to eventually have a specific contact person to escalate these delays to, many Bonitas members are not so lucky—and nobody paying medical aid premiums should have to fight every single month for life-sustaining medication, or beg for basic responses.

Bonitas is responsible for the service providers it forces members to use. It is unacceptable to hold back blood pressure medication because of administrative delays on separate items. I wish I had left sooner, as I kept hoping things would improve, but I have lost all trust in Bonitas. I am now paying out of pocket at a retail pharmacy while finalising the move of my family to another scheme, as it feels like Bonitas would rather pay for a hospitalisation caused by missed chronic medication than fix a broken system.
title: 20 years of loyalty ruined by Bonitas's chronic medication and service failures

Sent this email and still no response


Good day,

I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the handling of my medical aid claims and the lack of clarity surrounding my maternity benefits.

On 5 September, I submitted a claim for R700 for a prenatal consultation with my midwife. The claim was only partially paid, with Bonitas paying R157.95.

Since then, I have contacted Bonitas several times in an attempt to understand why the claim was only partially paid. Unfortunately, I have received conflicting information from different agents, with no satisfactory resolution to date.

For ease of reference, I have outlined the chronology of my interactions below:

16 September:
I was informed that my maternity benefits had not been activated, and therefore the claim had not been processed under these benefits. I explained that this was incorrect, as I had contacted Bonitas in August to activate my maternity benefits. I have attached the confirmation letter for reference.

The agent rechecked the system, confirmed that my maternity benefits were activated, and assured me that the claim would be resubmitted.

End of September:
I contacted Bonitas again and was informed that the resubmitted claim was still being processed.

October:
During another call, I was advised to expect payment on the following Friday, as this was the next payment run. However, no payment was received.

3 November:
I contacted Bonitas once again and was informed that the claim had been resubmitted. However, the scheme was still only paying R157.95. The agent explained that different tariffs apply to different prenatal consultations.

This explanation raises further concerns, as I have yet to receive a clear breakdown of the applicable tariffs, the benefits available to me, or the reason for the partial payment.

I have not submitted any further claims to date, as I have lost confidence in the clarity and consistency of the information provided by Bonitas. I am concerned that every claim will require multiple follow-up calls, with each agent providing a different explanation.

I have also requested that the recordings of my previous calls be retrieved and reviewed. To date, this has not been done.

What I require from Bonitas

As I prepare for the remainder of my pregnancy and the upcoming birth of my baby, I need a clear understanding of my maternity benefits so that I can plan financially and make informed decisions regarding my healthcare.

I would appreciate a comprehensive written breakdown of the following:

1. Prenatal consultations

What is the applicable tariff for each prenatal consultation with my midwife?

How many prenatal consultations am I covered for under my maternity benefits?

What amount will Bonitas pay per consultation, and what portion, if any, will I be expected to pay out of pocket?

Please provide a detailed explanation of the partial payment of R157.95 for my 5 September consultation.

2. Maternity facility and delivery costs

What portion of the facility fees for childbirth will Bonitas cover?

I previously contacted Bonitas to confirm whether Genesis Maternity Clinic is covered and was advised that it is. 

Please clarify exactly what is covered at Genesis Maternity Clinic and what costs I should expect to pay myself.

3. Healthcare professionals during childbirth
Please confirm whether my maternity benefits cover the fees of the following healthcare professionals during childbirth:

Midwife

Gynaecologist

Paediatrician

For each of these professionals, please provide the applicable tariff, the amount Bonitas will cover, and any potential shortfall that I may be required to pay.

4. Review of previous interactions
I would also like confirmation that my previous calls will be retrieved and reviewed, as I have repeatedly received conflicting information regarding my maternity benefits and the processing of my claim.

I believe it is reasonable to expect clear, accurate and consistent information regarding my medical aid benefits, particularly during a time when I need to plan for the healthcare needs of both myself and my baby.

The continued uncertainty has left me questioning whether I can rely on my medical aid to cover the benefits communicated to me.

I am therefore requesting that this complaint be escalated to the relevant department and that I receive a comprehensive written response addressing each of the above concerns.

I look forward to receiving a satisfactory resolution and clarity on my maternity benefits.

text:
I am writing to formally escalate a serious and increasingly urgent complaint regarding the ongoing issues I have experienced with Bonitas following my recent move from Discovery Medical Scheme to Bonitas.

My Bonitas membership number is ***.

When I joined Bonitas approximately three months ago, I specifically explained to the Askus Business Solutions sales team that my wife is diabetic and that continued access to her chronic diabetic medication was an essential requirement for us when considering a move from Discovery to Bonitas. We were assured that the appropriate chronic medication cover would be available and that there would be no issue maintaining her treatment.

Unfortunately, three months later, my wife is still struggling to obtain the required diabetic medication, and despite numerous calls, follow-ups and submissions, I have been unable to get this matter properly resolved.

Chronic medication issue

The process has been extremely frustrating and, more importantly, the ongoing delays are creating a serious medical concern for my wife.

We were not advised upfront that an HbA1c result would be required as part of the chronic medication approval process. After submitting the chronic medication prescription, I received no communication advising me that additional documentation was required. I only discovered this when I contacted the Chronic Department myself.

The required HbA1c results and supporting documentation were subsequently submitted immediately. More than a week passed without any communication or progress, requiring me to contact Bonitas again.

When I eventually called for an update, I was simply told that the person I was speaking to did not know what was happening. This is extremely concerning given that this relates to essential chronic medication.

I subsequently received a call from a representative named Nicole, who assured me that she would assist and email me so that I could respond with the valid HbA1c results and prescription. I was told that I simply needed to reply to her email with the required documentation.

Once again, no email was received.

I have exhausted every normal avenue of assistance

I have now gone far beyond what any member should reasonably be expected to do to obtain assistance.

I even went as far as lodging a complaint on HelloPeter in an attempt to get someone from Bonitas to take ownership of the matter. Despite doing this, nobody contacted me and nobody attempted to assist me.

I have contacted the sales team, the Chronic Department and the general enquiries teams repeatedly. None of these departments has been able to resolve the matter.

On numerous occasions I have specifically requested to speak to a manager or supervisor. Each time I have been told that the manager is "in a meeting" and cannot assist me.

This raises a very serious question: How bad does a member's situation have to become before someone at Bonitas takes ownership of the problem?

I have now reached the point where I have had to search for the CEO's email address simply because I cannot get assistance through the normal Bonitas channels.

That should not be necessary.

I should not have to escalate a medical and chronic medication issue to executive level simply to get someone to investigate why my wife's medication has not been properly dealt with after approximately three months.

During one of my calls with a consultant in the Chronic Department, I was particularly shocked by the attitude displayed. I was told that they could not assist me, and the consultant indicated that they did not care if I escalated the matter because they were not assisting me.

If this is an accurate reflection of how a Bonitas member can be treated when trying to obtain essential chronic medication, then I believe this requires urgent management investigation.

Membership suspension and payment issue

In addition to the chronic medication problem, I experienced a separate and extremely disruptive issue with my membership.

I was due to take my wife to the doctor, only to discover that my Bonitas membership had been suspended.

When I contacted Bonitas, I was advised that a payment was outstanding. My first payment was made by direct EFT because we had missed the relevant billing run. Proof of payment had already been provided to multiple departments, yet the payment had apparently not been captured on the system.

As a result, my wife was unable to attend her scheduled doctor's appointment.

After further calls and intervention, the payment issue was eventually resolved and the membership was reinstated.

This is another example of me having to repeatedly chase Bonitas to correct an issue that should have been resolved through the normal administrative process.

Impact on my wife's health

This is now much more than an administrative frustration.

My wife is diabetic and requires her medication as part of the ongoing management of her condition. Over the last three months, I have become increasingly concerned about the deterioration in her condition and the symptoms she is experiencing.

I am particularly concerned about increased nerve damage and numbness in her feet, as well as concerns regarding possible pancreatic complications. I am not making a medical diagnosis or claiming that every symptom is directly attributable to Bonitas' delays, but the continued interruption and difficulty obtaining her required medication is extremely concerning to me as her husband.

The consequences of uncontrolled or inadequately managed diabetes can be serious and can ultimately result in additional medical treatment, hospitalisation and significant costs.

What is particularly frustrating is that I have been paying my Bonitas premiums throughout this entire period while simultaneously having to spend thousands of rands of my own money attempting to obtain the medication privately because I cannot get the matter resolved through Bonitas.

I therefore have to ask:

What am I paying my medical aid premiums for if, when my wife needs essential chronic medication, I have to pay additional money out of my own pocket because nobody within Bonitas will take ownership of the problem?

Three months of unanswered calls and broken promises

For approximately three months, I have repeatedly been told:

Someone will call me back.
Someone will investigate the matter.
Someone will send me an email.
Someone will assist with the chronic medication.
A manager will deal with the issue.
The matter will be escalated.
Yet very little has actually happened without me repeatedly making another phone call.

I have spent an enormous amount of time trying to get assistance while watching my wife struggle with a medical condition that requires consistent treatment.

I would ask anyone reviewing this complaint to put themselves in my position for a moment:

If this were your wife, would you be satisfied watching her suffer while repeatedly being told that someone will assist, only for nobody to call back?

Would you accept being repeatedly transferred between departments, being unable to speak to a manager, receiving contradictory information and ultimately having to search for the CEO's contact details simply to get someone to listen?

I certainly do not.

Formal request for urgent investigation

I am therefore requesting that this matter be treated as a formal and urgent complaint and that it be escalated to an appropriate senior manager or executive who can take ownership of the matter.

I require the following:

Immediate escalation of my wife's chronic medication application.
Written confirmation of exactly what documentation is still outstanding, if anything.
Confirmation that all documentation already submitted has been received and correctly captured.
Urgent assistance in obtaining the required diabetic medication.
A written explanation as to why this matter has remained unresolved for approximately three months.
An explanation as to why we were not informed upfront about the HbA1c requirement.
An investigation into the handling of every previous call, submission and escalation relating to this matter.
An investigation into why my payment and proof of payment were not correctly captured, resulting in my membership being suspended.
An investigation into the conduct and service provided by the Askus Business Solutions sales team and the assurances given when we joined Bonitas.
An investigation into the responses and conduct of the Chronic Department consultants I have dealt with.
An explanation as to why I have repeatedly been unable to speak to a manager despite specifically requesting escalation.
A specific senior person to take ownership of this matter and communicate directly with me until it has been completely resolved.
A formal complaint reference number and confirmation of the escalation process from this point forward.
I have tried resolving this through the normal Bonitas channels for approximately three months.

I have contacted the sales team.

I have contacted the Chronic Department.

I have contacted general enquiries.

I have requested managers.

I have submitted documentation.

I have provided proof of payment.

I have followed up repeatedly.

I have even lodged a complaint on HelloPeter.

Still, nobody has taken ownership of the problem.

I am now escalating this directly because I have exhausted the normal channels available to me as a paying member.

I joined Bonitas based on the representations made to me when I was sold the membership, specifically after explaining that my wife's diabetic chronic medication was a critical requirement.

I expect Bonitas to investigate not only the current chronic medication problem, but also the entire chain of events that has resulted in a member being left for approximately three months without a satisfactory resolution.

This matter now requires urgent attention. My wife's health cannot continue to be placed in the middle of an administrative process where different departments simply pass the problem from one person to another.

Please acknowledge receipt of this complaint urgently, provide me with a formal complaint reference number, and confirm the name and contact details of the senior person who will take ownership of this matter.
